title: Tiered steady-state + burst SLOs for mixed-latency endpoints with tenant isolation and progressive rollout gates
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Purpose: Define a practical SLO surface and rollout gating strategy for mixed-latency Redwood endpoints (chat, streaming, embeddings) that explicitly separates steady-state expectations from burst behavior, supports per-tenant tiered contracts (Gold/Silver/Bronze), and integrates with runtime telemetry and Console rollout controls. This ticket is the PRD + acceptance criteria for the SLO definitions and the gating logic used during progressive releases.

Background: Existing SLO work covers single latency envelopes and rolling thresholds. Customers and platform teams need: (1) explicit burst-mode expectations so we can allow brief degradation under load without immediate rollback, (2) tenant-level SLO tiers to support committed capacity customers vs best-effort tenants, and (3) rollout gates that react to error-budget burn rate and burst-induced transient degradations differently than steady-state breaches.

Scope:
- Define numeric SLOs for steady-state and burst windows by endpoint type and tenant tier.
- Specify error budget calculation method and burn-rate thresholds for both windows.
- Produce concrete rollout gate rules (canary thresholds, ramp rules, automated rollback triggers).
- Define observability and synthetic checks required to validate SLOs during rollouts.
- List engineering dependencies and required telemetry fields (per-request service tags, KV cache hit rates, batching stats).

Out of scope: automated scaling policies for Dedicated (that remains an infra/ENG project), priced SLA contracts and legal wording. Those will follow SLO acceptance once numbers are locked.
acceptance_criteria: SLO spec exists as a single canonical doc with numeric targets for each endpoint type (chat/streaming/embeddings) and for each tenant tier (Gold/Silver/Bronze).
Steady-state latency SLOs defined as p50/p95/p99 for token-latency and request-latency where applicable, with separate first-token target for streaming chat.
Burst-window SLOs defined using a 5-minute sliding window that allows controlled degradations; burst-window targets documented and contrasted with steady-state.
Error budget calculation documented: 30-day rolling window for steady-state, separate 1-hour window for burst calculations; clear mapping from budget burn-rate to gate actions.
Rollout gates specified: initial canary (1% traffic, 24h) with hard abort rules, staged ramps (1%→10%→50%→100%) with minimum observation windows and allowed burst budget consumption per stage.

Automated rollback triggers listed and implementable by Console: e.g., sustained steady-state p95 breach exceeding 3x allowed burn-rate for 2 hours OR absolute increase in 5xx rate >0.5% over baseline for 30 minutes.
Console must be able to display per-tenant SLO status and per-stage gate health; mockup acceptance in Console design doc attached.
Synthetic harness exists and runs a representative traffic mix to validate SLOs before each major rollout; harness results consumed by rollout gates.

All telemetry fields required by the SLO logic are instrumented: request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, sequence_length_bucket, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, region_tag. ENG teams assigned to provide missing fields (see dependencies).
A short runbook describing triage steps and mitigation actions for common degradations is authored and linked from the SLO doc.
notes: Decision: split SLO surface into two orthogonal dimensions: steady-state (long-window SLA expectations) and burst-window (short transient tolerance). This reduces noisy rollbacks caused by predictable traffic spikes.

Rationale: committed tenants (Gold) get tighter steady-state targets and reserved capacity options; Silver/Bronze have looser steady-state targets but similar burst tolerances to avoid noisy cross-tenant impacts.
Trade-off: allowing burst degradation increases risk of transient user-visible slowdowns; mitigations include stricter canary abort thresholds and conservative initial ramps.
Telemetry ask: ENG-20345 to add kv_cache_hit and batch_size into per-request logs; ENG-20780 to add a SLO dashboard surface in Console; ENG-21456 to expose tenant-level traffic routing tags.
